A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same research work. Both contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete Appendices A–C, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on replay, feature geometry, and deep versus shallow forgetting, including benchmark evaluations and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Figures 2–6 and the experiments in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The replay procedure, architectures, and Neural Collapse/OOD modeling framework are unchanged. The revised linear-probe parameter concerns evaluation rather than the proposed approach.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CIFAR100, Tiny-ImageNet, CUB200, the CIFAR10 illustration, and the same class-, domain-, and task-incremental scenarios. Pretraining and feature-bottleneck coverage also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 11 retains DER, FDR, and iCaRL in the same comparisons. Figure 6 also retains the same LDA comparisons using population, identity-covariance, and buffer statistics.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 changes the reported scikit-learn logistic-regression probe setting from C=100 to C=10. This is a limited evaluation-setting revision; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. Other stated protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 retains the same pretraining, feature-bottleneck, and head-initialization ablations. The statistical-divergence analysis in Figure 6 and supplementary feature-geometry analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds [1000, 2000, 3000] in Appendix A.1 and retain the same uncertainty displays, including the ± reporting in Table 4. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The displayed results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains CIL shallow forgetting of 52.27 ± 2.41 and deep forgetting of 26.15 ± 1.92. No result updates accompany the revised probe setting.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix C retain the same definitions, hypotheses, propositions, asymptotic bounds, and proofs, including the OOD and replay separability results.

C1.justification: Despite the new title, the abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the replay efficiency gap, extending Neural Collapse to continual learning, and connecting forgetting to OOD geometry.

C2.justification: The covariance-deficiency and mean-inflation explanations are retained. Section 6 preserves the same limitations concerning asymptotic analysis, the idealized replay mixture, and unresolved multi-head interactions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 revises the documented probe hyperparameter from C=100 to C=10. The remaining implementation details, training configurations, preprocessing information, and codebase access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes Harun et al., 'What Variables Affect Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Pretrained Models?', from Section 5, Appendix B, and the bibliography. The associated discussion retains Kang et al. (2024), and the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled 'Heads collapse, features stay: Why Replay needs big buffers'. The header changes to ICLR 2026 publication status, the author footnote changes from corresponding authors to equal contribution, and a few wording and typography errors are corrected. Most prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 1 to page 2, reflowing the introduction, and Figure 5 is slightly enlarged. Their plotted content is unchanged; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The editorial and layout refinements leave the paper's results, theory, claims, and substantive limitations intact. The isolated C=100 to C=10 revision is unexplained and has no accompanying result changes demonstrating improved evaluation quality. Overall, the revision does not establish a meaningful gain or decline.
